relevance_reason: Review of congenital prothrombin deficiency covering its phenotypes, prevalence, gene, and mutation spectrum. Only the abstract was available.

findings.statement: Lancellotti and De Cristofaro (2009) reviewed congenital prothrombin deficiency and described 2 main phenotypes. Hypoprothrombinemia (type I deficiency) has low levels of both prothrombin activity and antigen. Dysprothrombinemia (type II deficiency) has normal or near-normal synthesis of a dysfunctional protein. Hypoprothrombinemia together with dysprothrombinemia had also been described in compound heterozygotes.
quotes: Two main phenotypes can be distinguished: (1) hypoprothrombinemia (type I deficiency), characterized by concomitantly low levels of activity and antigen; and (2) dysprothrombinemia (type II deficiency), characterized by the normal or near-normal synthesis of a dysfunctional protein.
In some cases, hypoprothrombinemia associated with dysprothrombinemia was also described in compound heterozygous defects.

findings.statement: Lancellotti and De Cristofaro (2009) stated that prothrombin deficiency is among the rarest inherited coagulation disorders, with a prevalence of about 1 in 2,000,000. No living patient with undetectable plasma prothrombin had been reported.
quotes: Prothrombin deficiency is among the rarest inherited coagulation disorders, with a prevalence of approximately 1:2,000,000.
No living patient with undetectable plasma prothrombin has been reported to date.

findings.statement: Lancellotti and De Cristofaro (2009) reported that 40 different mutations had been identified in prothrombin deficiency. Many clustered around the catalytic site, and another hot spot was in anion binding exosite I (the fibrinogen recognition site). More recently, mutations had also been found in the Na(+)-binding loop and in the thrombin light A chain. Most hypoprothrombinemia-associated mutations were missense, but nonsense mutations and 1 single-nucleotide deletion had also been described.
quotes: Forty different mutations have been identified and characterized in prothrombin deficiency. Many of them surround the catalytic site, whereas another "hot spot" is localized in the recognition domain called anion binding exosite I, also called fibrinogen recognition site.
Recently, mutations were identified also in the Na (+)-binding loop and in the light A-chain of thrombin.
Most hypoprothrombinemia-associated mutations are missense, but there are also nonsense mutations leading to stop codons and one single nucleotide deletion.

relevance_reason: This systematic review covers thrombophilia risk from factor V Leiden and the prothrombin G20210A variant. It does not deal with congenital prothrombin deficiency. Its prothrombin G20210A results give context only.

findings.statement: In a systematic review and meta-analysis of 46 articles, Segal et al. (2009) found that, in probands with venous thromboembolism, heterozygosity for prothrombin G20210A did not predict recurrent VTE compared with individuals without the variant (OR 1.45; 95% CI 0.96-2.2). They concluded that the evidence was insufficient on whether G20210A homozygosity predicts recurrent VTE and on the risk of VTE in family members of carriers.
quotes: Heterozygosity for prothrombin G20210A is not predictive of recurrent VTE in probands compared with individuals without prothrombin G20210A (OR, 1.45; 95% CI, 0.96-2.2).
Evidence is insufficient regarding the predictive value of prothrombin G20210A homozygosity for recurrent VTE and the risk of VTE in family members of individuals with prothrombin G20210A.

relevance_reason: Review of congenital prothrombin deficiency covering inheritance, prevalence, laboratory diagnosis, clinical features and treatment; no new patients.

findings.statement: Meeks and Abshire (2008) reviewed prothrombin (factor II) deficiency, a rare autosomal recessive coagulation disorder. Prothrombin is activated to thrombin, which cleaves fibrinogen to fibrin and contributes to a stable fibrin clot. They noted that more than 40 prothrombin mutations were known and that both hypoprothrombinemia and dysprothrombinemia had been described.
quotes: Prothrombin (factor II) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive coagulation disorder that occurs in approximately 1 in 1-2 million people.
There are more than 40 known mutations in prothrombin. Both hypoprothrombinemia and dysprothrombinemia have been described.

findings.statement: Meeks and Abshire (2008) stated that prothrombin deficiency occurs in about 1 in 1 to 2 million people.
quotes: Prothrombin (factor II) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive coagulation disorder that occurs in approximately 1 in 1-2 million people.

findings.statement: Meeks and Abshire (2008) noted that bleeding in prothrombin deficiency is mostly mucosal or follows surgery or trauma, but joint bleeding and intracranial hemorrhage had also been reported.
quotes: Clinical manifestations are predominantly mucosal or surgical- or trauma-associated bleeding, but joint bleeding and intracranial haemorrhages have been reported.

findings.statement: Meeks and Abshire (2008) noted that low prothrombin activity usually prolongs both the activated partial thromboplastin time and the prothrombin time. The hemostatic level of prothrombin is thought to be 20 to 40%, and its half-life is about 3 days.
quotes: Low prothrombin activity typically prolongs both the activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time.
The haemostatic level of prothrombin is thought to be between 20 and 40%, and the half-life is approximately 3 days.

findings.statement: Meeks and Abshire (2008) stated that no purified prothrombin products were available for replacement therapy. Fresh frozen plasma and prothrombin complex concentrates both contain prothrombin and may be used for treatment.
quotes: No purified prothrombin products are available for replacement therapy. Both fresh frozen plasma and prothrombin complex concentrates contain prothrombin and may be used for treatment.

relevance_reason: Reports nine novel prothrombin (F2) gene mutations in 13 patients with hypoprothrombinemia or dysprothrombinemia, with structural analysis of how they cause disease.

findings.statement: Akhavan et al. (2000) described prothrombin deficiency as an autosomal recessive disorder with a moderately severe bleeding tendency.
quotes: Prothrombin deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder associated with a moderately severe bleeding tendency.

findings.statement: Akhavan et al. (2000) screened the prothrombin gene in 13 patients with prothrombin deficiency and found 9 novel candidate mutations. Of the 11 patients with hypoprothrombinemia, 10 were homozygous for 5 mutations and 1 was a compound heterozygote. The 2 patients with dysprothrombinemia were homozygous for 2 mutations. Eight mutations were missense: Arg-1Gln and Arg-2Trp in the propeptide, Asp118Try in kringle-1, Arg220Cys in kringle-2, and Gly330Ser, Ser354Arg, Arg382His and Arg538Cys in the serine protease domain. The ninth was an in-frame 3-bp deletion that removed one amino acid (del Lys301/302).
quotes: 13 patients with prothrombin deficiency were screened for the presence of alterations in the prothrombin gene, and nine novel candidate mutations were identified
Of 11 patients with hypoprothrombinemia, ten are homozygous for five mutations and one patient is a compound heterozygote. The two patients with dysprothrombinemia are homozygous for two mutations.
The ninth mutation is an in-frame deletion of 3 bp that results in the omission of one amino acid (del Lys 301/302).

findings.statement: Akhavan et al. (2000) mapped the missense mutations onto crystal structures of alpha-thrombin and prothrombin fragments 1 and 2. They inferred that the hypoprothrombinemia mutations affected cleavage of the propeptide from the Gla domain, the stability of kringle-1 and kringle-2, or the close association of the A and B chains of the serine protease domain. They inferred that the dysprothrombinemia mutations directly impaired catalytic function because they lie at the active site crevice or exosite 1 of the serine protease domain.
quotes: The hypoprothrombinemia mutations were inferred to affect either the cleavage of the propeptide from the Gla domain, the stability of the kringle-1 and -2 domains, or the close association of the A and B chains of the serine protease domain.
The dysprothrombinemia mutations were inferred to directly affect catalytic function through their location at the active site crevice or exosite 1 within the serine protease domain.

relevance_reason: The paper reports a dysprothrombinemia patient (prothrombin Denver) who is a compound heterozygote for two prothrombin missense mutations, with clinical and functional characterization.

findings.statement: Lefkowitz et al. (2000) described the original patient with prothrombin Denver. The patient had a severe hemophilia-like bleeding disorder and was treated with weekly prophylactic factor replacement. Factor II activity was 5 units/dl and factor II antigen was 21 units/dl, consistent with moderately severe dysprothrombinemia.
quotes: The original patient with prothrombin Denver had a severe haemophilia-like bleeding disorder treated with weekly prophylactic factor replacement.
Analysis of factor II activity and antigen in the patient showed a factor II activity of 5 units/dl and factor II antigen of 21 units/dl.

findings.statement: In the prothrombin Denver patient, Lefkowitz et al. (2000) sequenced PCR-amplified prothrombin exons (the entire thrombin portion, exons VIII-XIV, and exons I-II and IV-VII) and found compound heterozygosity for two different Glu-to-Lys point mutations, glu300-to-lys and glu309-to-lys. DNA was also obtained from the patient's mother and brother.
quotes: This moderately severe dysprothrombinaemia was found to be associated with compound heterozygosity for two different Glu-->Lys point mutations, at amino acid positions 300 and 309.
Genomic DNA from the patient, mother and brother was obtained from peripheral blood white cells.

findings.statement: Lefkowitz et al. (2000) assayed plasma from the prothrombin Denver proband, and the results suggested that the functional defect was in the activation of the zymogen to the enzyme.
quotes: Assays of plasma from the prothrombin Denver proband suggested that the functional defect was in the activation of zymogen to enzyme.

findings.statement: Lefkowitz et al. (2000) noted that dysprothrombinemia is a rare congenital cause of bleeding, and that fewer than 25 families with a functional prothrombin (factor II) defect had been reported.
quotes: Dysprothrombinaemia is a rare, congenital cause of bleeding. Fewer than 25 families who express a functional prothrombin (factor II) defect have been reported.

relevance_reason: A review of congenital prothrombin deficiency and dysprothrombinemia covering diagnosis, factor II levels, bleeding symptoms and treatment.

findings.statement: Girolami et al. (1998) noted that Quick et al. first described prothrombin (factor II) deficiency in 1947, and that Shapiro et al. reported the first prothrombin abnormality in 1969. The condition is still considered very rare.
quotes: Prothrombin (factor II) deficiency was first described in 1947 by Quick et al., although the first prothrombin abnormality was reported in 1969 by Shapiro et al. The condition is still considered very rare.

findings.statement: Girolami et al. (1998) stated that prothrombin deficiency or abnormality can be diagnosed with a combination of clotting, chromogenic and immunologic assays. In true deficiency, all assays decrease in parallel whatever the activating agent. Discrepancies among clotting assays, particularly with viper venoms, suggest dysprothrombinemia. The authors stated that cases with a parallel decrease in prothrombin activity and antigen should not be considered examples of hypoprothrombinemia.
quotes: In cases of true deficiency, a parallel decrease in all these assays is observed, regardless of the activating agent. If discrepancies among the clotting assays are noted, particularly using viper venoms, a dysprothrombinemia should be suspected.
Cases with a parallel decrease in prothrombin activity and antigen should not be considered as examples of hypoprothrombinemia.

findings.statement: Girolami et al. (1998) reported that factor II activity is usually less than 10% of normal in homozygotes for true deficiency and 40 to 60% in heterozygotes. In congenital dysprothrombinemia, factor II levels are more variable, usually 1 to 50% of normal, because patients may be homozygotes, heterozygotes, or compound heterozygotes. Compound heterozygotes may carry an abnormality plus a true deficiency, or two distinct abnormalities. Antigen levels in dysprothrombinemia are normal, near normal or slightly decreased, but always higher than clotting activity.
quotes: Usually, activity levels less than 10% of normal are found in homozygotes, and between 40 and 60% in heterozygotes.
Usually the levels of factor II vary between 1 and 50% of normal.
Antigen levels in congenital dysprothrombinemias will be normal, near normal or slightly decreased but always higher than the clotting counterpart.

findings.statement: Girolami et al. (1998) reported that bleeding can be severe in homozygous true prothrombin deficiency, with hemarthroses and intracranial bleeding described. Bleeding is more variable in dysprothrombinemias, and heterozygotes are usually asymptomatic. Prognosis is variable and generally matches the prothrombin activity level.
quotes: Bleeding manifestations may be severe in homozygous 'true' deficiency and may be more variable in dysprothrombinemias. Heterozygotes are usually asymptomatic.
In homozygous true deficiency, hemarthroses and intracranial bleeding have been described.

findings.statement: Girolami et al. (1998) stated that substitution therapy uses prothrombin complex concentrates or plasma. Because infused prothrombin has a long half-life of about 70 hours, hemostatically effective levels of about 50% of normal are easily achieved.
quotes: Substitution therapy is based on the administration of prothrombin complex concentrates or of plasma. The long half-life of prothrombin injected, about 70 h, allows the achievement of hemostatically effective levels (about 50% of normal) without difficulty.

findings.statement: Girolami et al. (1998) noted that the prothrombin gene is located on chromosome 11 and is composed of 10 exons. They reported that molecular studies have found several point mutations in some dysprothrombinemias.
quotes: The gene involved in the synthesis of prothrombin is located in chromosome 11. It is composed of 10 exons and 8 introns. Molecular biology studies have discovered several point mutations in some of the dysprothrombinemias.

relevance_reason: Reports a homozygous missense prothrombin (F2) mutation causing severe hypoprothrombinemia with autosomal recessive inheritance and segregation in a family.

findings.statement: Poort et al. (1994) described a male patient with a severe bleeding tendency and hypoprothrombinemia (factor II activity 2%, factor II antigen 5%). Five homozygous brothers and sisters of the propositus were also clinically affected, with severe hemorrhages including epistaxis and soft tissue, muscle, and joint bleeding in all, and severe hemorrhages in the 2 women.
quotes: A patient with a severe bleeding tendency and hypoprothrombinemia (Factor II activity 2%, Factor II antigen 5%) was screened for the presence of alterations in his prothrombin gene.

Only the five homozygous brothers and sisters of the propositus were clinically affected (severe hemorrhages including epistaxis, soft tissue, muscle and joint bleedings in all, and severe hemorrhages in the two women).

findings.statement: In a patient with severe hypoprothrombinemia, Poort et al. (1994) identified by direct sequencing of the prothrombin gene a homozygous A-to-G substitution in exon 3, predicting a tyr44-to-cys (Y44C; TAC-to-TGC) substitution. Both parents were heterozygous, and family studies showed complete cosegregation of the mutation with prothrombin deficiency; only the homozygous sibs were clinically affected.
quotes: revealed that the patient was homozygous for an A-->G substitution in exon 3. This substitution predicts the replacement of Tyr44 (TAC) by Cys (TGC) in the prothrombin molecule.
Both parents were found to be heterozygous for the same mutation. Further family studies revealed complete cosegregation of the mutation with the prothrombin deficiency.

findings.statement: Poort et al. (1994) concluded that the bleeding tendency in this family appeared to be inherited as an autosomal recessive trait, since only homozygous family members were clinically affected and the parents were heterozygous.
quotes: The bleeding tendency therefore seems to inherit as an autosomal recessive trait.

relevance_reason: Case report of a new dysprothrombin variant (prothrombin Houston) with clinical and biochemical characterization, directly relevant to dysprothrombinemia.

findings.statement: Weinger et al. (1980) described a 72-year-old man with a lifelong history of easy bruisability and posttraumatic bleeding who had a prolonged prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time. His plasma Stypven, Taipan, and Echis carinatus venom clotting times were also prolonged. The variant was named prothrombin Houston.
quotes: A 72-yr-old male with a lifelong history of easy bruisability and posttraumatic bleeding had a prolonged prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time.
His plasma Stypven, Taipan, and Echis carinatus venom clotting times were prolonged.

findings.statement: Weinger et al. (1980) confirmed a dysprothrombin in their patient by a discrepancy between plasma prothrombin coagulant activity and prothrombin antigen levels. The prothrombin was fully adsorbed to and eluted from barium sulfate, and on crossed immunoelectrophoresis it resembled normal prothrombin, but crossed immunoelectrofocusing showed the patient's prothrombin antigen was more basic than normal.
quotes: The presence of a dysprothrombin was confirmed by the discrepancy between plasma prothrombin coagulant activity and prothrombin antigen levels.
His plasma prothrombin was capable of being completely absorbed onto and then eluted from barium sulfate.
demonstrated that the patient's prothrombin antigen was more basic than normal.

findings.statement: Weinger et al. (1980) found that the patient's barium sulfate eluate, activated by Echis carinatus venom, clotted purified fibrinogen more slowly than normal eluate, although SDS gel electrophoresis showed the prothrombin was cleaved by the venom. They suggested that the coagulopathy of prothrombin Houston results from the generation of a dysfunctional thrombin.
quotes: when reacted with Echis carinatus venom (which directly cleaves prothrombin to thrombin) clotted purified fibrinogen at a rate slower than normal plasma eluate.
SDS-slab gel electrophoresis revealed that the prothrombin present in the patient's eluate was cleaved by Echis carinatus venom.
These studies suggest that the coagulopathy of prothrombin Houston results from the generation of a dysfunctional thrombin.

relevance_reason: The paper describes a new dysprothrombinemia (prothrombin Gainesville) in identical twins, with clinical and laboratory characterization.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (1981) described a pair of identical twins with dysprothrombinemia (prothrombin Gainesville) who were evaluated for menometrorrhagia and mild postoperative bleeding. Each twin had a slightly prolonged partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time. Apart from this, the full hemostatic evaluation was normal.
quotes: A pair of identical twins was evaluated for menometrorrhagia and mild post-operative bleeding. Each had a slightly prolonged partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (1981) found that plasma prothrombin activity in the identical twins with prothrombin Gainesville was 23% and 25% of normal by a Russell's viper venom assay. However, each twin had 70% of normal plasma prothrombin antigen, which indicated a dysprothrombinemia. The authors stated that prothrombin Gainesville was the twelfth such dysprothrombin reported.
quotes: Full hemostatic evaluation was normal, except that plasma prothrombin activity was 23% and 25% of normal with a Russell's viper venom assay. Each twin had 70% of normal plasma prothrombin antigen.
Prothrombin Gainesville is the twelfth such disorder reported.

findings.statement: Smith et al. (1981) obtained prothrombin kinetic data in the twins before and during hysterectomy. Infused prothrombin (Konyne) had a volume of distribution of about 1.5 times the plasma volume and a half-life of 34 hours.
quotes: Prothrombin kinetic data were obtained before and during hysterectomy. In these twins, infused prothrombin (Konyne) was found to have a volume of distribution of approximately one and one-half times the plasma volume and a half-life of 34 hours.

relevance_reason: The paper describes a French family with a mild bleeding tendency in which hypoprothrombinemia and dysprothrombinemia both occurred, three of the children carrying both. It also reports a new prothrombin variant, prothrombin Metz.

findings.statement: Josso et al. (1982) studied a French family with a mild hemorrhagic tendency. The father was heterozygous for hypoprothrombinemia and the mother was heterozygous for dysprothrombinemia. All possible genetic combinations were seen among the children, and 3 of them were double heterozygotes.
quotes: Investigation of a mild hemorrhagic tendency in a French family revealed the father to be heterozygous for hypoprothrombinemia while the mother was heterozygous for dysprothrombinemia.
All possible genetic combinations could be demonstrated.

findings.statement: Josso et al. (1982) identified an abnormal prothrombin, which they named prothrombin Metz, in 3 children of a French family who were double heterozygotes. Each child carried hypoprothrombinemia inherited from the father and dysprothrombinemia inherited from the mother.
quotes: Among the children the double heterozygosity encountered in 3 of them allowed us to discover an abnormal prothrombin, prothrombin Metz

findings.statement: Josso et al. (1982) found that prothrombin Metz generated an abnormal thrombin. This thrombin was less sensitive to inactivation by antithrombin III than normal thrombin.
quotes: which generates an abnormal thrombin less sensitive to inactivation by antithrombin III than normal thrombin

relevance_reason: Describes electrophoretic structural variants of prothrombin (FII), one polymorphic in Pacific Islanders, with variation localized to the profragment; relevant to prothrombin variant/heterogeneity context.

findings.statement: Board et al. (1982) described a new electrophoretic procedure for localizing prothrombin that revealed 3 allelic variants at the prothrombin structural locus (FII). In each case, investigation of the activated products showed that the structural variation was located on a profragment and not on the enzymatically active thrombin molecule.
quotes: This technique has revealed three allelic variants at the prothrombin structural locus (FII).

Investigation of the activated products of the three variant prothrombins has demonstrated that, in each case, the structural variation is located on a profragment and not on the enzymically active thrombin molecule.

findings.statement: Board et al. (1982) found that one prothrombin electrophoretic variant allele, FII4, reached polymorphic frequencies in some Pacific Island populations.
quotes: One of these alleles (FII4) reaches polymorphic frequencies in some Pacific Island populations.

relevance_reason: Functional characterization of the dysfunctional thrombin derived from the prothrombin variant Metz (a dysprothrombinemia); no patient clinical or variant data in the abstract.

findings.statement: Rabiet et al. (1984) purified thrombin Metz, made by activating the variant prothrombin Metz with factor Xa in the presence of calcium, phospholipid, and factor Va. By physicochemical criteria it was identical to normal thrombin. It had less than 4% of normal fibrinogen clotting activity, abnormal Km and Kcat on S2238, and only 34% of normal DAPA fluorescence enhancement. It was less than 5% as effective as normal thrombin at inducing platelet aggregation.
quotes: By physicochemical criteria, thrombin Metz is identical to normal thrombin.
Thrombin Metz exhibits less than 4% of fibrinogen clotting activity. Both Km and Kcat, determined on S2238, are abnormal.
Thrombin Metz is less than 5% as effective as normal thrombin in inducing platelet aggregation.

findings.statement: Rabiet et al. (1984) found that thrombin Metz released both fibrinopeptides A and B more slowly than normal, with fibrinopeptide B more affected, which led to slow fibrin polymerization. Its interaction with antithrombin III was slower than normal, but not in the presence of heparin. Thrombin Metz also bound less tightly to heparin-Sepharose, and heparin inhibited its activity on S2238 less strongly. The authors predicted that the defect affects the catalytic site or its vicinity and, jointly or consequently, the region that interacts with antithrombin III and heparin.
quotes: A decreased release rate for both fibrinopeptides, more marked for fibrinopeptide B, results in a slow fibrin polymerization

Interaction with antithrombin III is slower than normal when followed by SDS gel electrophoresis and inhibition of the amidolytic activity of thrombin on S2238. This abnormality is not observed in the presence of heparin.
we can predict that the defect in thrombin Metz affects the catalytic site or its vicinity and, jointly or consequently, the region of interaction of thrombin with antithrombin III and heparin.

relevance_reason: Reports a Cuban family with congenital dysprothrombinemia (prothrombin Habana) and compound heterozygosity for a dysfunctional prothrombin and a true prothrombin deficiency.

findings.statement: Rubio et al. (1983) described a Cuban family with congenital dysprothrombinemia (prothrombin Habana). The proband, a 5-year-old girl, had umbilical bleeding after birth, then easy bruising and a bleeding tendency throughout her life. Her prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time were prolonged.
quotes: A Cuban family with a new congenital dysprothrombinaemia is described.
The propositus was a 5-year-old female who presented with umbilical bleeding after birth followed by easy bruising and bleeding tendency throughout her life.
The main laboratory features of the defect included prolongation of prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time.

findings.statement: Rubio et al. (1983) found that the proband's prothrombin activity was below 10% in several one- and two-stage assays, whereas staphylocoagulase-complexed prothrombin and immunologic methods gave levels of about 50%. The abnormal prothrombin migrated more anodically on single and two-dimensional immunoelectrophoresis, and adding calcium did not change its migration.
quotes: Prothrombin activity was less than 10% in several one- and two-stage systems. However, the staphylocoagulase-complexed prothrombin level and immunologic methods yielded levels of about 50%.
The migration of the abnormal prothrombin was more anodic in single and bidimensional immunoelectrophoresis system and did not change by the addition of calcium.

findings.statement: In family studies, Rubio et al. (1983) found that the father had about 50% prothrombin activity and antigen (a true deficiency). The mother had 45% prothrombin activity but about 100% prothrombin antigen (a dysfunctional prothrombin). The authors suggested that the proband was heterozygous for an abnormal prothrombin and heterozygous for true prothrombin deficiency.
quotes: Family studies revealed that the father had approximately 50% prothrombin activity and antigen, whereas the mother had 45% prothrombin activity but about 100% prothrombin antigen.
We suggest that the propositus is heterozygous for an abnormal prothrombin and heterozygous for true prothrombin deficiency.

relevance_reason: The title shows the paper is about congenital dysprothrombinemia, which is included in this entry. Only the title was available, so no patient, variant or laboratory details could be extracted.

findings.statement: Shirakami and Kawauchi (1984) reported on congenital dysprothrombinemia.
quotes: Congenital dysprothrombinemia.

findings.statement: Lanchantin et al. (1968) studied the amino acid composition of human plasma prothrombin.
quotes: Amino acid composition of human plasma prothrombin.

relevance_reason: Original description of a family with congenital dysprothrombinemia (structurally abnormal prothrombin), directly characterising the included dysprothrombinemia phenotype.

findings.statement: Shapiro et al. (1969) studied a large family in which 11 members had half-normal plasma levels of biologic prothrombin activity but normal quantities of immunoreactive prothrombin, whose immunologic properties appeared identical to those of the normal zymogen.
quotes: A large family has been studied, 11 of whose members have half-normal plasma concentrations of biological prothrombin activity.
affected family members have been shown to possess normal quantities of immunoreactive prothrombin, whose immunologic properties seem identical with those of the normal zymogen.

findings.statement: Shapiro et al. (1969) found the pattern of inheritance of dysprothrombinemia in the family to be autosomal, and suggested that affected individuals were heterozygotes.
quotes: The pattern of inheritance is autosomal.
These results suggest that affected individuals are heterozygotes in whom half the prothrombin molecules synthesized are structurally abnormal

findings.statement: Shapiro et al. (1969) isolated prothrombin from the plasma of an affected individual and obtained normal protein yields but half-normal prothrombin activity; activation via intrinsic and extrinsic systems, concentrated sodium citrate, or trypsin yielded half or less of the expected thrombin clotting and esterase activities. During clotting all prothrombin-mobility material disappeared, and serum immunoelectrophoresis showed a normal 'pro piece' plus an additional activation product of intermediate mobility.
quotes: Prothrombin isolation from the plasma of one such individual gave normal yields of protein but half-normal amounts of prothrombin activity.
gives rise to half, or less, of the thrombin clotting and esterase activities expected from a comparable normal prothrombin preparation.

Immunoelectrophoresis of the serum reveals a normal nonthrombin "pro piece," and an additional activation product with an electrophoretic mobility intermediate between that of prothrombin and of "pro piece."

findings.statement: Shapiro et al. (1969) concluded that in affected heterozygotes half of the synthesized prothrombin molecules are structurally abnormal, undergoing some alterations during activation but being incapable of releasing active thrombin.
quotes: half the prothrombin molecules synthesized are structurally abnormal, since they undergo some alterations during activation, but are incapable of releasing the active enzyme, thrombin.

findings.statement: Girolami (1971) studied the hereditary transmission of congenital 'true' hypoprothrombinemia.

findings.statement: Josso et al. (1971) described a congenital abnormality of the prothrombin (factor II) molecule, which they called prothrombin Barcelona, in 4 sibs.
quotes: Congenital abnormality of the prothrombin molecule (factor II) in four siblings: prothrombin Barcelona.

findings.statement: Kattlove et al. (1970) reported on hereditary prothrombin deficiency.
quotes: Hereditary prothrombin deficiency.

relevance_reason: The title reports a new congenital dysprothrombinemia (prothrombin Padua), which falls within this entry's included phenotype. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Girolami et al. (1974) described prothrombin Padua, which they called a 'new' congenital dysprothrombinemia.
quotes: Prothrombin padua: a "new" congenital dysprothrombinemia.

relevance_reason: Describes a new structurally abnormal prothrombin variant (dysprothrombinemia) in a Mexican family, which fits the included dysprothrombinemia subject.

findings.statement: Valls-de-Ruiz et al. (1987) found a functionally normal but structurally abnormal prothrombin variant in a Mexican family and named it prothrombin 'Mexico City.' On immunoisoelectric focusing, the variant had a more acidic isoelectric point (4.01) than normal prothrombin (4.29). Its molecular weight on SDS-PAGE was normal. Two-dimensional immunoelectrophoresis showed abnormal cleavage by factor Xa and by Echis carinatus venom, although both produced functionally normal thrombin. Calcium binding and overall antigenic structure were normal.
quotes: A functionally normal but structurally abnormal prothrombin variant was found in a Mexican family.

Immunoisoelectricfocusing studies revealed that this variant has a more acidic isoelectric point (4.01) than normal prothrombin (4.29), but it proved to have a normal molecular weight as assessed by sodium-dodecyl-sulphate polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis.

Two-dimensional immunoelectrophoresis studies showed an abnormal cleavage of the prothrombin molecule by factor Xa and Echis carinatus venom as well, despite the fact that both yield functionally normal thrombin molecules.

findings.statement: Valls-de-Ruiz et al. (1987) suggested that prothrombin Mexico City results from a simple substitution or translocation mutation at the level of fragment 2. They considered the variant different from previously described prothrombin variants.
quotes: These results taken together suggest a simple (substitution or translocation) mutation at the fragment 2 level.
Since this prothrombin variant is different from others described previously, the name "Mexico City" is proposed to identify it.

findings.statement: Valls-de-Ruiz et al. (1987) described prothrombin Mexico City as an asymptomatic prothrombin variant with autosomal dominant inheritance.
quotes: Prothrombin "Mexico City," an asymptomatic autosomal dominant prothrombin variant.

relevance_reason: Describes a dysprothrombinemia variant (prothrombin Tokushima): proband plasma studies and biochemical characterization of the dysfunctional thrombin.

findings.statement: Inomoto et al. (1987) purified a mutant prothrombin, designated prothrombin Tokushima, from the plasma of a proband with 12% of normal plasma prothrombin clotting activity and 42% of normal prothrombin antigen. The purified variant had the same SDS-PAGE mobility as normal prothrombin, and its proteolysis catalyzed by factor Xa was identical to that of normal prothrombin.
quotes: A mutant prothrombin, designated prothrombin Tokushima, was purified from plasma of a proband with 12% of normal plasma clotting activity and 42% of normal prothrombin antigen.
The factor Xa-catalyzed proteolysis of prothrombin Tokushima examined by SDS-PAGE was found to be identical to that of "prothrombin."

phenotypes.text: reduced prothrombin clotting activity (12% of normal)

findings.statement: Inomoto et al. (1987) found that thrombin Tokushima, generated by factor Xa activation, had normal molecular weight but less than 22% of normal clotting activity and a kcat/Km toward a fluorogenic substrate less than one-tenth of normal, although active-site titration showed no difference from normal thrombin. Thrombin Tokushima was 2.5% as effective as normal thrombin in inducing platelet aggregation and 33% as effective in forming a complex with antithrombin III. The authors concluded that the molecular defect resides in the thrombin portion of the prothrombin and that binding sites for various substrates appear greatly impaired.
quotes: Thrombin Tokushima exhibited less than 22% of normal clotting activity, and the value of kcat/Km (mumol/L-1 second-1) was less than one tenth of that of "thrombin" when Boc-Val-Pro-Arg-4-methylcoumaryl-7-amide was used as a substrate.
Thrombin Tokushima was 2.5% as effective as "thrombin" in inducing platelet aggregation.
These results indicate that the molecular defect resides in the thrombin portion of prothrombin Tokushima and that the binding sites for various substrates appear to be greatly impaired.

relevance_reason: The paper describes a new congenital dysprothrombinemia (prothrombin Poissy) in a newborn who was presumed homozygous, along with a family study of heterozygous relatives.

findings.statement: Dumont et al. (1987) described a newborn girl with congenital dysprothrombinemia (prothrombin Poissy) who had severe bleeding from the second day of life. Prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time were very prolonged.
quotes: A new congenital dysprothrombinaemia is described in a newborn baby girl who presented severe bleeding from the second day of life.
Routine coagulation tests showed very prolonged prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time

findings.statement: In the proband, Dumont et al. (1987) found prothrombin activity of about 2% in a one-stage assay. Activity was 35% with staphylocoagulase and 25% with Echis carinatus venom. Prothrombin antigen was 47%, and the protein migrated abnormally on crossed immunoelectrophoresis. In a thrombin generation system free of natural inhibitors, the abnormal prothrombin was activated slowly and incompletely. The authors called it a 'lazy' dysprothrombin.
quotes: with about 2% prothrombin activity in a one-stage assay. Staphylocoagulase and Echis carinatus venom prothrombin assays were respectively 35% and 25%.
The prothrombin antigen level was 47% and its migration in crossed immuno-electrophoresis was abnormal.
Thrombin generation in a system free from natural inhibitors showed that the abnormal prothrombin was slowly and incompletely activated.

findings.statement: In a family study, Dumont et al. (1987) found both normal and abnormal prothrombin in the plasma of the proband's father, mother, and brother. They suggested that the proband was homozygous for the dysprothrombin.
quotes: Family study revealed the presence of both normal and abnormal prothrombin in the plasma of three family members: the father, the mother and the brother.
The propositus is thought to be homozygous for a 'lazy' dysprothrombin.

relevance_reason: Reports a family with a new congenital dysprothrombinemia (prothrombin Segovia), with clinical, coagulation and immunologic characterization.

findings.statement: Rocha et al. (1986) described a 21-year-old man with congenital dysprothrombinemia who presented with hemarthrosis of the left knee together with an extensive hematoma after minor trauma. His prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time were prolonged. His parents were consanguineous.
quotes: The propositus is a 21-yr-old man who presented simultaneously with hemartrosis of the left knee and an extensive hematoma following a minor trauma. Prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time were prolonged.
Family studies revealed consanguinity between the propositus' mother and father

phenotypes.hpo_label: Bleeding with minor or no trauma

findings.statement: Rocha et al. (1986) found that the propositus had very low prothrombin activity with physiological activators (7% by one-stage and 20% by two-stage assay), Russell viper venom-cephalin (23%), Notechis scutatus scutatus venom (15%) and Echis carinatus venom (17%). By contrast, levels were borderline to normal with Taipan venom (64%) and normal by staphylocoagulase and immunologic methods, which points to a dysfunctional prothrombin molecule.
quotes: Prothrombin activity was very low when measured by biological assay using physiological activators (7% by one-stage method and 20% by two-stage method) or a Russel's viper venom-cephalin mixture (23%), Notechis scutatus scutatus venom (15%) and Echis carinatus venom (17%)
in contrast, the level was found to be borderline to normal using Taipan viper venom (64%) and normal by both staphylocoagulase and immunologic methods.

phenotypes.text: reduced prothrombin activity with normal antigen

findings.statement: Rocha et al. (1986) found that the propositus's consanguineous parents both had prothrombin levels reduced by 50% when physiological activators or Echis carinatus venom were used. This is consistent with both parents being heterozygous carriers.
quotes: Family studies revealed consanguinity between the propositus' mother and father and both presented a 50% reduced prothrombin level when physiological activators or Echis carinatus viper venom were used.

findings.statement: Rocha et al. (1986) observed a line of identity between normal and abnormal prothrombin on immunodiffusion. The abnormal prothrombin migrated less anodically, and adding calcium did not change its migration. On bidimensional immunoelectrophoresis the patient's serum showed 3 bands, compared with 2 in normal serum. The authors proposed the name prothrombin Segovia for this variant.
quotes: A line of identity between normal and abnormal prothrombin was observed on immunodiffusion. The migration of the abnormal prothrombin was less anodic and was not changed by the addition of calcium.

The patient's serum showed 3 bands in the bidimensional immunoelectrophoresis system, whereas normal serum showed only 2 bands. The term prothrombin Segovia is proposed to define this new prothrombin abnormality.

relevance_reason: The paper describes a family with inherited dysprothrombinemia (prothrombin Magdeburg), a qualitative prothrombin variant that falls under this entry.

findings.statement: Lutze et al. (1989) described dysprothrombinemia (prothrombin Magdeburg) in 7 members of 1 family spanning 3 generations. Five of the 7 had a slightly increased bleeding tendency, seen mainly as heavier or prolonged bleeding after trauma and surgery.
quotes: Seven members of one family over three generations were found to have
Five of the seven persons had a slightly increased bleeding tendency which manifested itself especially in more marked or prolonged posttraumatic and postoperative bleedings.

findings.statement: Lutze et al. (1989) found that in the affected family members, the ratio of factor II clotting activity to factor II concentration was reduced to about 0.5. This reduction was not seen when prothrombin was measured after activation with staphylocoagulase. SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis showed 'normal' prothrombin plus 2 abnormal prothrombins with higher molecular weights and lower isoelectric points.
quotes: a characteristic reduction to about 0.5 of the ratio between factor II clotting activity and factor II concentration, which was not seen when measuring prothrombin after activation with staphylocoagulase
In addition to the "normal" prothrombin, two abnormal prothrombins, with higher molecular weights and lower isoelectric points, were found by SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis.

phenotypes.text: reduced ratio of factor II activity to factor II antigen

findings.statement: Lutze et al. (1989) concluded that prothrombin Magdeburg is an autosomal hereditary dysprothrombinemia and that the affected persons are heterozygotes.
quotes: This is an autosomal hereditary dysprothrombinemia, the affected persons being heterozygotes.

relevance_reason: The paper reports a dysprothrombinemia patient (Prothrombin Himi) who is compound heterozygous for two new missense mutations in the prothrombin gene.

findings.statement: Morishita et al. (1992) described Prothrombin Himi, an inherited dysfunctional prothrombin. It had reduced fibrinogen clotting activity but kept full hydrolytic activity toward synthetic substrates.
quotes: A congenitally dysfunctional form of prothrombin, Prothrombin Himi, shows reduced fibrinogen clotting activity, although it retains full hydrolytic activity toward synthetic substrates.

phenotypes.text: dysprothrombinemia with reduced fibrinogen clotting activity

findings.statement: In a female proband with Prothrombin Himi, Morishita et al. (1992) amplified exons 8 to 14 of the prothrombin gene by PCR and screened them by SSCP analysis. Sequencing then found compound heterozygosity for two new point mutations in exon 10. The first was a T-to-C transition at nucleotide 8751 that changed methionine to threonine at codon 337 (Met337Thr; Thrombin Himi I), inherited from the father. The second was a G-to-A transition at nucleotide 8904 that changed arginine to histidine at codon 388 (Arg388His; Thrombin Himi II), inherited from the mother. One of the proband's sisters also inherited both variant alleles.
quotes: One is a T to C transition at position 8751, resulting in the substitution of threonine for methionine at codon 337 (Thrombin Himi I).
By sequencing analysis of her parents, it was determined that Thrombin Himi I was inherited from the father and Thrombin Himi II from the mother.
One variant allele detected in the father was inherited by the proband and one of her sisters, and the other detected in the mother was also inherited by them.

variants.as_reported: Met-337-->Thr (Thrombin Himi I); T to C transition at position 8751

findings.statement: Morishita et al. (1992) found that the Prothrombin Himi proband's second prothrombin allele carried a G-to-A transition at nucleotide 8904 in exon 10. This change replaced arginine with histidine at codon 388 (Arg388His; Thrombin Himi II) and was inherited from her mother. Together with Met337Thr from her father, it made the proband compound heterozygous for two dysfunctional prothrombin molecules.
quotes: The other is a G to A transition at 8904, resulting in the substitution of histidine for arginine at codon 388 (Thrombin Himi II).
These results confirm that Prothrombin Himi is compound heterozygous for two dysfunctional prothrombin molecules.

variants.as_reported: Arg-388-->His (Thrombin Himi II); G to A transition at 8904

relevance_reason: Reports the molecular basis (Arg418Trp) of a dysprothrombinemia variant, prothrombin Tokushima, and describes its maternal inheritance and carrier detection.

findings.statement: Iwahana et al. (1992) used PCR-SSCP, PCR-RFLP and sequencing of PCR-amplified genomic DNA to study the dysprothrombinemia variant prothrombin Tokushima. They found a C-to-T substitution at nucleotide 9,490 that changed arginine to tryptophan at position 418 (Arg418Trp) and abolished an MspI site. The proband had inherited the mutant gene from the mother. The authors considered this point mutation the likely molecular basis because Southern blot analysis showed no distinct changes, the variant gene product had the same molecular weight as the abnormal protein, and the proteolytic peptide fragments showed no other amino acid abnormalities.
quotes: Sequencing analysis using PCR-amplified genomic DNA clarified a substitution of thymine (T) for cytosine (C) at position 9,490, changing arginine (Arg) to tryptophan (Trp) at position 418 of the polypeptide chain.

The abnormal gene was detected by altered migration by PCR-SSCP and by the loss of an MspI site by PCR-RFLP. The gene for prothrombin Tokushima was shown to be inherited from the mother of the proband.
This point mutation is assumed to be the molecular basis of prothrombin Tokushima, firstly, because of the absence of distinct changes in Southern blot analysis of the proband's DNA

variants.as_reported: prothrombin Tokushima; C-to-T at position 9,490, Arg418Trp

findings.statement: Iwahana et al. (1992) concluded that PCR-SSCP and PCR-RFLP (loss of an MspI site) were useful for detecting the abnormal prothrombin gene and for direct diagnosis of carrier status in dysprothrombinemia. The authors stated that this was the first report of gene analysis of dysprothrombinemia.
quotes: It is concluded that PCR-SSCP and PCR-RFLP were useful for detecting the abnormal gene and for directly diagnosing the carrier status of dysprothrombinemia.
This is the first report of gene analysis of dysprothrombinemia.

relevance_reason: Reports the molecular basis of a compound heterozygote for dysprothrombinemia (prothrombin Tokushima) and hypoprothrombinemia, including a frameshift null allele in F2 inherited from the father.

findings.statement: Iwahana et al. (1992) analyzed the prothrombin gene in a proband who was a compound heterozygote for dysprothrombinemia (prothrombin Tokushima) and hypoprothrombinemia. Using PCR-SSCP with endonuclease digestion and mutated primer-mediated PCR-RFLP, they detected a single nucleotide substitution responsible for prothrombin Tokushima, along with three polymorphisms.
quotes: The molecular and genetic basis of a compound heterozygote for dys- and hypoprothrombinemia was analyzed.
A single nucleotide substitution responsible for dysprothrombinemia of prothrombin Tokushima was detected, as were three polymorphisms.

findings.statement: Iwahana et al. (1992) identified the hypoprothrombinemia allele in the compound heterozygous proband as a single base insertion of thymine at position 4177 in exon 6 of the prothrombin gene, found by PCR-SSCP with endonuclease digestion and genomic sequencing. The frameshift altered the amino acid sequence from codon 114 and created a premature TGA stop at codon 174 in exon 7; because exon 7 encodes the kringle 2 domain preceding the thrombin sequence, the authors concluded this leads to a null prothrombin phenotype. Inheritance of this allele from the father was demonstrated.
quotes: Sequencing of PCR-amplified genomic DNA revealed a single base insertion of thymine (T) at position 4177. The resulting frameshift mutation caused both an altered amino acid sequence from codon 114 and a premature termination codon (i.e., TGA) at codon 174 in exon 7.
Because exon 7 encodes the kringle 2 domain preceding the thrombin sequence, this frameshift leads to the null prothrombin phenotype.
The inheritance of the hypoprothrombinemia gene from the father to the proband was proved by PCR-SSCP with endonuclease digestion and mutated primer-mediated PCR-RFLP.

variants.as_reported: single base insertion of thymine (T) at position 4177

relevance_reason: Describes a new dysprothrombinemia (prothrombin Quick) and a true hypoprothrombinemia patient, and reviews the reported families with congenital prothrombin deficiency.

findings.statement: Owen et al. (1978) restudied one of the first patients identified by Quick and colleagues as having a plasma prothrombin defect. She had about half the normal amount of prothrombin antigen but almost no prothrombin function. The authors proposed calling this dysprothrombin 'prothrombin Quick.'
quotes: One of the first patients previously identified by Quick and his associates as having a defect in her plasma prothrombin has been shown to have about half the normal amount of prothrombin antigen but virtually no prothrombic function.
We propose that this dysprothrombin be designated prothrombin Quick.

phenotypes.text: virtually absent prothrombin function with about half-normal prothrombin antigen

findings.statement: Owen et al. (1978) found that a second patient first described by Quick had true hypoprothrombinemia, lacking both functional and antigenic prothrombin.
quotes: An additional patient also first described by Quick was found to be truly hypoprothrombinemic--that is, to lack both functional and antigenic prothrombin.

phenotypes.text: lack of functional and antigenic prothrombin

findings.statement: Owen et al. (1978) reviewed the reported inherited prothrombin defects. There were 10 families with hypoprothrombinemia (true reductions of prothrombin), 6 families with dysprothrombinemia (functionally abnormal prothrombin), and 8 more families with a prothrombin abnormality that had not yet been classified.
quotes: Only 10 families with significant reductions of this plasma protein (hypoprothrombinemia) have been observed. Even fewer, six families, have been found to have a functionally abnormal prothrombin (dysprothrombinemia) in their blood.
An as yet undefined prothrombin abnormally has been recognized in eight other families.

relevance_reason: Only the title was available. It describes a biochemical study of how the dysprothrombin variant prothrombin Barcelona is activated, which is relevant to dysprothrombinemia.

findings.statement: Rabiet et al. (1979) studied the activation of the abnormal prothrombin variant prothrombin Barcelona and reported evidence that active high molecular weight intermediates form during its activation.
quotes: Activation of prothrombin Barcelona. Evidence for active high molecular weight intermediates.
